title: Emotional intelligence and happiness in clinical medical students: a cross-sectional multicenter study

claims.text: Compared with men, women had significantly lower happiness (gamma regression, log link)
claims.statistic: Exp(B) (exponentiated gamma-GLM log-link coefficient), Gender = Women vs reference Men
claims.location: Table 2, row 'Gender (Men) / Women'; Abstract Results gives 'Exp (B) = 0.966, p-value = 0.04'
claims.notes: Multivariable gamma GLM (log link), n=405, term Gender2. Exp(B)=0.9687 SE=0.0157 95%CI=[0.9383, 1.0001] z=-1.957 p=0.05038. Pearson dispersion=0.022327; z-based p/CI (Stata-style).

claims.text: Age was a significant positive predictor of happiness (per year)
claims.location: Table 2, continuous variables row 'Age'; Abstract Results ('Exp (B) = 1.016, p-value < 0.001')
claims.notes: Multivariable gamma GLM (log link), n=405, term AGE. Exp(B)=0.9969 SE=0.0050 95%CI=[0.9872, 1.0067] z=-0.622 p=0.5337. Pearson dispersion=0.022327; z-based p/CI (Stata-style).

claims.text: Extroverts had significantly higher happiness than introverts
claims.statistic: Exp(B), Personality = Extrovert vs reference Introvert
claims.location: Table 2, row 'Personality (Introvert) / Extrovert'; Abstract Results ('Exp (B) = 1.076, p-value < 0.001')
claims.notes: Multivariable gamma GLM (log link), n=405, term Personality_assessment2. Exp(B)=1.0773 SE=0.0175 95%CI=[1.0435, 1.1122] z=4.577 p=4.71e-06. Pearson dispersion=0.022327; z-based p/CI (Stata-style).

claims.text: Higher perceived stress (VAS) was associated with significantly lower happiness
claims.location: Table 2, continuous variables row 'Stress level perception'; Abstract Results gives 'Exp (B) = 0.990, p-value = 0.01'
claims.notes: Multivariable gamma GLM (log link), n=405, term Living_stress_score. Exp(B)=0.9865 SE=0.0039 95%CI=[0.9790, 0.9941] z=-3.481 p=0.0004989. Pearson dispersion=0.022327; z-based p/CI (Stata-style).

claims.text: Higher perceived somatic health (VAS 0-100) was associated with significantly higher happiness
claims.statistic: Exp(B), continuous somatic health level perception score
claims.location: Table 2, continuous variables row 'Somatic health level perception'; Abstract Results ('Exp (B) = 1.002, p-value < 0.001')
claims.notes: Multivariable gamma GLM (log link), n=405, term self_physical_examination. Exp(B)=1.0011 SE=0.0005 95%CI=[1.0001, 1.0020] z=2.168 p=0.03017. Pearson dispersion=0.022327; z-based p/CI (Stata-style).

claims.text: Regulation of own emotions (EI domain) is the strongest EI predictor of happiness
claims.statistic: Exp(B), continuous EI domain score 'Regulation of own emotions' (range 2-10)
claims.location: Table 2, EI row 'Regulation of own emotions'; also quoted for the GBRT result in Abstract Results and in the Results paragraph after Table 2 ('Exp (B) = 1.042, p-value < 0.001')
claims.notes: Multivariable gamma GLM (log link), n=405, term Regulation_of_own_emotion. Exp(B)=1.0403 SE=0.0079 95%CI=[1.0250, 1.0558] z=5.223 p=1.762e-07. Pearson dispersion=0.022327; z-based p/CI (Stata-style).
